3.1.  Inpatient Care
We will indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred on the Insured Person's Hospitalization during the Policy Period upto sum insured and 
within limitations noted, following an Illness or Injury that occurs during the Policy Period, provided that:
a) Hospitalization is Medically Necessary and advised by Medical Practitioner and the treatment follows Evidence Based Clinical 
Practices and Standard Treatment Guidelines.
b) The Medical Expenses incurred are Reasonable and Customary Charges for one or more of the following:
     i. Room Rent for General Ward;
          ii. Nursing charges for nursing services under Hospitalization through a qualiﬁed nursing staﬀ asas an Inpatient;
     iii. Medical Practitioners' fees, excluding any charges or fees for Standby Services;
     iv. Physiotherapy, investigation and diagnostics procedures directly related to the current event which lead to Hospitalization;
     v. Medicines, drugs as prescribed by the treating Medical Practitioner related to the current event that led to Hospitalization and not 
otherwise;
     vi. Intravenous ﬂuids, blood transfusion, injection administration charges, consumables and/or enteral feedings;
     vii. Operation theatre charges;
     viii. The cost of prosthetics and other devices or equipment, if implanted internally during Surgery;
     ix. Intensive / Critical Care Unit Charges;
     x. Ancillary hospital charges;
     xi. Implants as per hospital policy or clinical conditions.

proportion of the difference between the Room Rent for General Ward and the availed category of room.

3.2.  Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses
We will indemnify the Insured Person's Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred following an Illness or Injury that occurs during 
the Policy Period provided that:
a) We have accepted a claim for Inpatient Care under Section 3.1 (Inpatient Care) or Section 3.4 (Day Care Treatment) or Section 3.9
 (Alternative Treatments) or Section 3.10 (Technological Advancements & Treatments) and Pre- hospitalization Medical Expenses ar
e incurred for the same condition for which We have accepted the Inpatient Care or Day Care Treatment or Alternative Treatments or 
Technological Advancements & Treatments claim.
b) We will not be liable to pay Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person's
 admission  for  Inpatient  Care/  Day  Care  Treatment/  Alternative  Treatments/  Technological  Advancements  &  Treatments  or  such 
expenses incurred prior to inception of the First Policy with Us.
c) Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses can be claimed under the Policy on a Reimbursement basis only.
d) Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred on Physiotherapy will also be payable provided that such Physiotherapy is Medically
 Necessary and advised by the Medical Practitioner and such Physiotherapy is directly related to current event that led to Hospitalization 
or Day Care Treatment.

& Treatments claim has been incurred shall be reduced.
3.3.  Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses

 (Alternative Treatments) or Section 3.10 (Technological Advancements & Treatments) and Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses ar
e incurred for the same condition for which We have accepted the Inpatient Care or Day Care Treatment or Alternative Treatments or 
Technological Advancements & Treatments claim.
b) We will not be liable to pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person's
 admission  for  Inpatient  Care/  Day  Care  Treatment/  Alternative  Treatments/  Technological  Advancements  &  Treatments  or  such 
expenses incurred prior to inception of the First Policy with Us.
c)  Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses can be claimed under the Policy on a Reimbursement basis only. 
d) Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred on Physiotherapy will also be payable provided that such Physiotherapy is Medically
 Necessary and advised by the Medical Practitioner and such Physiotherapy is directly related to current event that led to Hospitalization 
or Day Care Treatment.
e) Sum Insured for the Policy Year in which In-patient Care/ Day Care Treatment/ Alternative Treatments/ Technological Advancements 
& Treatments claim has been incurred shall be reduced.

5. Healthcare Provider
All the benefits under this policy shall be applicable for coverage only at Network Provider. 
The coverage shall be extended to Non-network Provider only in the below mentioned scenarios:
a) All cases of emergency as defined in Section 2.1.16
b) Treatment not available at Network Provider.
c) Insured Person travelling to a location where Network Provider is not accessible. In this scenario, Insured Person must submit a proof of 
travel and reason of travel with evidence which shall be accepted by Us.
d) Insured Person relocating to a location where Network Provider is not accessible. In this scenario, the Insured Person must submit the Proof 
of Address of the new relocated address within 2 months of relocation or at time of claim, whichever is lesser.
6. Co-payment
For all types of benefits and its coverage under this policy, there is no Co-Payment applicable to the Insured Person, except for the below 
mentioned scenario:
a) A Co-payment of 10% shall be applicable, if the Insured Person is seeking coverage at Non-Network healthcare provider due to either of 5
 (b), 5 (c), and 5 (d) as defined in Healthcare Provider (Section 5), and does not intimate Us 48 hours prior to the time of admission.a) A Co-payment of 10% shall be applicable, if the Insured Person is seeking coverage at Non-Network healthcare provider due to either of 5 (b), 5 (c), and 5 (d) as defined in Healthcare Provider (Section 5), and does not intimate Us 48 hours prior to the time of admission.
b) A Co-payment of 10% shall be applicable, if the Insured Person is seeking coverage at Non-Network healthcare provider due to scenario as defined in 5 (a) as defined in Healthcare Provider (Section 5), and does not intimate Us within 24 hours from the time of admission.
b) If We have accepted a claim under this beneﬁt, We will also indemnify the Insured Person's Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses 
and Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses in accordance with Sections 3.2 and 3.3 till the overall Sum Insured.

1. NARAYANA ADITI: COMPREHENSIVE HOSPITALIZATION COVERAGE  
 
Narayana Aditi provides a comprehensive hospitalization coverage and discretionary discounts for OPD services at our services. 
Please note the following: 
 
a) 
The coverage outside Network Provider (Annexure 2) is limited basis the Plan opted at the time of purchase. It can ONLY be 
availed in the below scenarios, otherwise it is NOT COVERED. 
 
i. 
All cases of emergency. Emergency means a serious medical condition or symptom resulting from Illness or Injury which 
arises suddenly and unexpectedly and requires immediate care and treatment by a Medical Practitioner to prevent death or 
serious long-term impairment of the Insured Person's health. 
 
Explanation: An unforeseen, sudden, and acute medical condition that arises without prior warning and requires immediate 
medical attention to prevent serious jeopardy to the insured person’s life, significant impairment to bodily functions, or 
permanent dysfunction of any body organ or part. 
 
The condition must be of such severity that a prudent layperson with average knowledge of health and medicine would 
reasonably expect that failure to seek immediate care could result in: 
• 
Serious risk to life; 
• 
Permanent disability; or 
• 
Serious and irreversible harm to health. 
 
Exclusions: Conditions not meeting the criteria for immediate and critical care, such as routine medical issues, elective 
procedures, or symptoms that are chronic, mild, or manageable through outpatient care, do not constitute an Emergency. 
 
ii. 
Treatment not available at Network Provider. 
 
iii. 
Insured Person travelling to a location where Network Provider is not accessible. In this scenario, Insured Person must 
submit a proof of travel and reason of travel with evidence which shall be accepted by Us. 
 
iv. 
Insured Person relocating to a location where Network Provider is not accessible. In this scenario, the Insured Person must 
submit the Proof of Address of the new relocated address within 2 months of relocation or at time of claim, whichever is 
lesser. 
 
b) 
Health check-up / examination plays a critical role in delivering the true sense of comprehensive coverage that the Plan offers. The 
Insured Persons (for both individual and family floater policies) aged 18 years and above can choose to undergo health check-up 
/ examination either before Policy issuance or within 90 days of Policy Issuance. This choice will have an impact on applicable 
Waiting Periods and Premium. This is not applicable for POS – Aditi and POS – Aditi Plus. 
 
c) 
There are 6 plans available for the Proposer (subject to availability for sales at several geographical locations) – Plan 1, Plan 2, 
Plus (Access to Preferred + Verified Provider Network) and Prime (Access to Preferred + Verified + Other Provider Network), POS 
– Aditi and POS – Aditi Plus. 
 
Premium Illustration is exhibited in Annexure 9. Please read the Prospectus carefully before you purchase the policy. 
 
2. WHO CAN AVAIL BENEFITS OF THIS POLICY  
 
Under this policy, following can be covered: 
a) 
A person and his/her family members including his/her spouse, upto 4 dependent children less than 25 years of age and both 
parents or parents-in-law. 
b) 
Residing in the serviceable location as determined and amended from time to time by the Company. 
c) 
The entry ages for the principal beneficiary of Certificate of Insurance is from 18 years (last birthday). The range of entry ages for 
dependent children are from 3 months to 25 years. 
d) 
Please note if any Insured Person who is a child and has completed 26 years at the time of Renewal, then such Insured Person 
will have to take a separate policy based on Our underwriting guidelines, as he/she will no longer be eligible to be covered under 
the Policy as a dependent child. In such cases, the credit of the Waiting Periods served under the issued Certificate of Insurance 
will be passed on to the separate Policy taken by such Insured Person.

1. Preamble 
 
This is a contract of insurance between You and Us which is subject to the payment of the full premium in advance and the terms, conditions, 
and exclusions to this Policy. This Policy has been issued on the basis of the Disclosure to Information Norm, including the information 
provided by You in respect of the Insured Persons in the Proposal Form and the Customer Information Sheet. 
 
Please inform Us immediately of any change in the address or any other changes aﬀecting You or any Insured Person. 
 
Note: The terms listed in Section 2 (Deﬁnitions) and used elsewhere in the Policy in Initial Capitals shall have the meaning set out against 
them in Section 2 wherever they appear in the Policy. 
 
2. Definitions 
 
For the purposes of interpretation and understanding of this Policy, We have deﬁned herein below some of the important words used in the 
Policy and for the remaining language and the words; they shall have the usual meaning as described in standard English language 
dictionaries. The words and expressions deﬁned in the Insurance Act 1938, IRDA Act 1999, Regulations, Circulars and Guidelines issued by 
the IRDAI, as amended from time to time, shall carry the meanings explained therein. 
 
Note: Where the context permits, the singular will be deemed to include the plural, one gender shall be deemed to include the other genders 
and references to any statute shall be deemed to refer to any replacement or amendment of that statute. 
 
2.1 Standard Deﬁnitions 
 
2.1.1 
Accident or Accidental means a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, visible and violent means. 
 
2.1.2 
Associated Medical Expenses shall include Room Rent, nursing charges, Medical Practitioners' fees and operation theatre 
charges. 
 
2.1.3 
AYUSH Day Care Centre means and includes Community Health Centre (CHC), Primary Health Centre (PHC), Dispensary, 
Clinic, Polyclinic or any such health centre which is registered with the local authorities, wherever applicable and having 
facilities for carrying out treatment procedures and medical or surgical/para-surgical interventions or both under the 
supervision of registered AYUSH Medical Practitioner(s) on day care basis without in-patient services and must comply with 
all the following criterion:  
a. 
Having qualified registered AYUSH Medical Practitioner (s) in charge;  
b. 
Having dedicated AYUSH therapy sections as required and/or has equipped operation theatre where surgical procedures 
are to be carried out;  
c. 
Maintaining daily records of the patients and making them accessible to the Insurance company’s authorized 
representative. 
 
2.1.4 
AYUSH Treatment refers to the medical and / or hospitalization treatments given under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, 
Unani, Sidha and Homeopathy systems. 
 
2.1.5 
AYUSH Hospital: An AYUSH Hospital is a healthcare facility wherein medical/surgical/para surgical treatment procedures and 
interventions are carried out by AYUSH Medical Practitioner(s) comprising of any of the following: 
 
a. 
Central or State Government AYUSH Hospital; or 
b. 
Teaching Hospital attached to AYUSH College recognized by the Central Government/Central Council of Indian 
Medicine/Central Council of Homeopathy; or 
c. 
AYUSH Hospital, standalone or co-located with In-patient healthcare facility of any recognized system of medicine, 
registered with the local authorities, wherever applicable, and is under the supervision of a qualiﬁed registered AYUSH 
Medical Practitioner and must comply with all the following criterion: 
i. 
Having at least 5 in-patient beds 
ii. 
Having qualiﬁed AYUSH Medical Practitioner in charge round the clock; 
iii. 
Having dedicated AYUSH therapy sections as required and/or has equipped operation theatre where 
surgical procedures are to be carried out; 
iv. 
Maintaining daily records of the patients and making them accessible to the insurance company's 
authorized representative

3. Base Benefits  
 
The Beneﬁts available under this Policy are described below. 
 
a. 
The Policy covers Reasonable and Customary Charges incurred towards medical treatment or consultation taken by the Insured 
Person during the Policy Period for an Illness, Injury or conditions as described in the sections below, provided such Illness, Injury 
or conditions contracted or sustained by an Insured Person during the Policy Period. The Beneﬁts listed in the sections below will 
be payable subject to the terms, conditions and exclusions of this Policy and the availability of the Sum Insured and always subject 
to any sub-limits in respect of that Beneﬁt as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule for the Insured Person. 
 
b. 
All the Beneﬁts (including Optional Covers and Value-Added Services) under the product have been summarized in the Policy 
Schedule as illustrated in Annexure 1. 
 
c. 
All claims for any beneﬁts under the Policy must be made in accordance with the process deﬁned under Section 11 (Claim 
Procedure). 
 
d. 
All claims paid under any beneﬁt except for those paid under Section 3.7 (Health Checkup) shall reduce the Sum Insured for that 
Policy Year in which the claim has been incurred, unless otherwise speciﬁed in the respective section and only the balance Sum 
Insured after payment of claim amounts admitted shall be available for all future claims arising in that Policy Year. 
 
3.1 
Inpatient Care 
 
We will indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred on the Insured Person's Hospitalization during the Policy Period following an Illness 
or Injury that occurs during the Policy Period, provided that: 
 
a. 
Hospitalization is Medically Necessary and advised by Medical Practitioner and the treatment follows Evidence Based Clinical 
Practices and Standard Treatment Guidelines.  
 
b. 
The Medical Expenses incurred are Reasonable and Customary Charges for one or more of the following: 
i. 
Room Rent for General Ward unless selected otherwise as part of the Optional Cover "Room Category Modification 
Option" or the category of the room at respective Network Provider that is in-built with the Plan as illustrated in Annexure 
1. 
ii. 
Nursing charges for nursing services under Hospitalization through a qualiﬁed nursing staﬀ as an Inpatient; 
iii. 
Medical Practitioners' fees, excluding any charges or fees for Standby Services; 
iv. 
Physiotherapy, investigation and diagnostics procedures directly related to the current event which lead to 
Hospitalization; 
v. 
Medicines, drugs as prescribed by the treating Medical Practitioner related to the current event that lead to Hospitalization 
and not otherwise; 
vi. 
Intravenous ﬂuids, blood transfusion, injection administration charges, consumables and/or enteral feedings; 
vii. 
Operation theatre charges; 
viii. 
The cost of prosthetics and other devices or equipment, if implanted internally during Surgery; 
ix. 
Intensive / Critical Care Unit Charges; 
x. 
Ancillary hospital charges; 
xi. 
Implants as per hospital policy or clinical conditions. 
 
c. 
If the Insured Person chooses to get admitted in higher category room that General Ward, access to which is only permitted if the 
optional cover “Enhance Access to Provider Network” as described in Section 4.6, is opted or in-built with any Plan, We shall be 
liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses (including surcharges or taxes thereon) in the 
proportion of the difference between the Room Rent for eligible room category and the availed category of room. 
 
d. 
Proportionate deductions shall not be applicable for hospitals which do not follow differential billing or for those expenses in respect 
of which differential billing is not adopted based on the room category. 
 
e. 
We shall not be liable to pay the visiting fees or consultation charges for any Medical Practitioner visiting the Insured Person unless 
such: 
i. 
Medical Practitioner's treatment or advice has been sought by the Hospital; and  
ii. 
Visiting fees or consultation charges are included in the Hospital's bill

We will not be liable to pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 90 days or 180 days (if the Optional Cover:

Provider Network and Verified Provider Network listed in Annexure 2A and 2B respectively and Other Provider Network (if “Enhance 
Access to Provider Network” is opted or in-built with any Plan) listed in Annexure 2C, immediately post the Insured Person's 
discharge from the hospital for Inpatient Care/ Day Care Treatment/ Alternative Treatments/ Modern Treatments or such expenses 
incurred prior to inception of the First Policy with Us. 
 
c. 
Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses can be claimed under the Policy on a Reimbursement basis only. 
 
d.

a. 
The Policy covers Reasonable and Customary Charges incurred towards medical treatment or consultation taken by the Insured 
Person during the Policy Period for an Illness, Injury or conditions as described in the sections below, provided such Illness, Injury 
or conditions contracted or sustained by an Insured Person during the Policy Period. The Beneﬁts listed in the sections below will 
be payable subject to the terms, conditions and exclusions of this Policy and the availability of the Sum Insured and always subject 
to any sub-limits in respect of that Beneﬁt as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule for the Insured Person.

Schedule as illustrated in Annexure 1. 
 
c.

d.

shall be available for all future claims arising in that Policy Year. 
 
3.1 
Inpatient Care 
 
We will indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred on the Insured Person's Hospitalization during the Policy Period following an Illness 
or Injury that occurs during the Policy Period, provided that: 
 
a. 
Hospitalization is Medically Necessary and advised by Medical Practitioner and the treatment follows Evidence Based Clinical 
Practices and Standard Treatment Guidelines.  
 
b. 
The Medical Expenses incurred are Reasonable and Customary Charges for one or more of the following: 
i. 
Room Rent for 
a. 
any Room Category subject to availability at actuals at Preferred Provider Network and Verified Provider 
Network listed in Annexure 2A and 2B respectively 
b. 
Private Room (as defined in Section 2.2.23) at Other Provider Network listed in Annexure 2C, if the optional 
cover “Access to Other Provider Network” is opted or in-built with any Plan 
c. 
Private Room (as defined in Section 2.2.23) at Non-Network Provider, for eligible and admissible cases as laid 
down is Section 6 (Healthcare Provider) 
ii. 
Nursing charges for nursing services under Hospitalization through a qualiﬁed nursing staﬀ as an Inpatient; 
iii. 
Medical Practitioners' fees, excluding any charges or fees for Standby Services; 
iv. 
Physiotherapy, investigation and diagnostics procedures directly related to the current event which lead to 
Hospitalization; 
v. 
Medicines, drugs as prescribed by the treating Medical Practitioner related to the current event that lead to Hospitalization 
and not otherwise; 
vi. 
Intravenous ﬂuids, blood transfusion, injection administration charges, consumables and/or enteral feedings; 
vii. 
Operation theatre charges; 
viii. 
The cost of prosthetics and other devices or equipment, if implanted internally during Surgery; 
ix. 
Intensive / Critical Care Unit Charges; 
x. 
Ancillary hospital charges; 
xi. 
Implants as per hospital policy or clinical conditions. 
 
c.

room.

dictionaries. The words and expressions deﬁned in the Insurance Act 1938, IRDA Act 1999, regulations notiﬁed by the IRDAI and circulars

2.1.1 
Accident or Accidental means a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, visible and violent means. 
 
2.1.2 
AYUSH Treatment refers to the medical and / or hospitalization treatments given under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, 
Unani, Sidha and Homeopathy systems. 
 
2.1.3 
AYUSH Hospital: An AYUSH Hospital is a healthcare facility wherein medical/surgical/para surgical treatment procedures and 
interventions are carried out by AYUSH Medical Practitioner(s) comprising of any of the following: 
 
a. 
Central or State Government AYUSH Hospital; or 
b. 
Teaching Hospital attached to AYUSH College recognized by the Central Government/Central Council of Indian

c. 
AYUSH Hospital, standalone or co-located with In-patient healthcare facility of any recognized system of medicine, 
registered with the local authorities, wherever applicable, and is under the supervision of a qualiﬁed registered AYUSH 
Medical Practitioner and must comply with all the following criterion: 
i. 
Having at least 5 in-patient beds 
ii.

iii.

surgical procedures are to be carried out; 
iv. 
Maintaining daily records of the patients and making them accessible to the insurance company's 
authorized representative 
 
2.1.4

charges. 
 
2.1.5 
Cashless Facility means a facility extended by the insurer to the insured where the payments of the costs of treatment 
undergone by the insured in accordance with the policy terms and conditions, are directly made to the network provider by 
the insurer to the extent pre-authorization is approved. 
 
2.1.6 
Congenital Anomaly means a condition which is present since birth and which is abnormal with reference to form, structure, 
or position. 
 
a.

b. 
External Congenital Anomaly: Congenital Anomaly which is in the visible and accessible parts of the body.

3.1 
In-Patient Care 
 
We will indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred on the Insured Person's Hospitalization during the Policy Period following an Illness 
or Injury that occurs during the Policy Period, provided that: 
 
a. 
Hospitalization is Medically Necessary and advised by Medical Practitioner and the treatment follows Evidence Based Clinical 
Practices and Standard Treatment Guidelines.  
 
b. 
The Medical Expenses incurred are Reasonable and Customary Charges for one or more of the following: 
i. 
Room Rent for Room Type as specified in Certificate of Insurance / Schedule of Benefits 
ii. 
Nursing charges for nursing services under Hospitalization through a qualiﬁed nursing staﬀ as an In-Patient; 
iii. 
Medical Practitioners' fees, excluding any charges or fees for Standby Services; 
iv. 
Physiotherapy, investigation and diagnostics procedures directly related to the current event which lead to 
Hospitalization; 
v. 
Medicines, drugs as prescribed by the treating Medical Practitioner related to the current event that lead to Hospitalization 
and not otherwise; 
vi. 
Intravenous ﬂuids, blood transfusion, injection administration charges, consumables and/or enteral feedings; 
vii. 
Operation theatre charges; 
viii. 
The cost of prosthetics and other devices or equipment, if implanted internally during Surgery; 
ix. 
Intensive / Critical Care Unit Charges; 
x. 
Ancillary hospital charges; 
xi. 
Implants as per hospital policy or clinical conditions. 
 
c. 
If the Insured Person chooses to get admitted in higher category room other than the eligible Room Type for eligible cases of 
admissions, We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses (including surcharges or 
taxes thereon) in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent for the eligible category as specified in the Certificate of 
Insurance / Policy Schedule and the availed category of room. 
 
d. 
We shall not be liable to pay the visiting fees or consultation charges for any Medical Practitioner visiting the Insured Person unless 
such: 
i. 
Medical Practitioner's treatment or advice has been sought by the Hospital; and  
ii. 
Visiting fees or consultation charges are included in the Hospital's bill 
 
 
3.2 
Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses 
 
We will indemnify the Insured Person's Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred following an Illness or Injury at Network Providers 
as listed out in Annexure 2 and updated on our website from time to time, that occurs during the Policy Period provided that: 
 
a. 
We have accepted a claim under Section 3.1 (In-Patient Care) or Section 3.4 (Day Care Treatment) or Section 3.5 (Living Organ 
Donor Transplant) or Section 3.7 (Alternative Treatments) or Section 3.8 (Technological Advancements and Treatments) and Pre-
hospitalization Medical Expenses are incurred for the same condition for which We have accepted the In-Patient Care or Day Care 
Treatment or Alternative Treatments or Technological Advancements & Treatments or Living Organ Donor Transplant claim. 
 
b. 
We will not be liable to pay Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses beyond the period specified in the Certificate of Insurance / Policy 
Schedule immediately preceding the Insured Person's admission for In-Patient Care / Day Care Treatment / Alternative Treatments/ 
Technological Advancement and Treatments / Living Organ Donor Transplant or such expenses incurred prior to inception of the 
First Policy with Us. 
 
c. 
Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses can be claimed under the Policy on a Reimbursement basis only. 
 
d. 
Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred on Physiotherapy will also be payable provided that such Physiotherapy is Medically 
Necessary and advised by the Medical Practitioner and such Physiotherapy is directly related to the current event that led to 
Hospitalization or Day Care Treatment. 
 
e. 
Sum Insured for the Policy Year in which In-patient Care/ Day Care Treatment/ Alternative Treatments/ Technological 
Advancements & Treatments claim has been incurred shall be reduced.

findings.finding: V2 wording title/footer prints NHIHLIP25035V022425; current/older registers print NHIHLIP25036V022425. Visible p25 disclaimer prints NHIHLIP25035V012425 while same-page footer prints the V2 identifier. Keep all assertions and document bytes, do not normalize one away.
findings.effect: Family and V2-labelled document identity supported; exact regulatory UIN/version identity needs authoritative resolution.

evidence.locator: Aditi and Arya cards and document anchors

findings.finding: Production product page still displays Aditi V5 and Arya V1 UIN labels but links Aditi V6/Arya V2 wordings, CIS and prospectuses. Re-fetching both register URLs returns unchanged 12-row/eight-row bytes. Newer originals establish version candidates, not their launch/effective dates.
findings.effect: Do not infer current publication/applicability solely from product card, filename, register snapshot or highest UIN.

findings.finding: Arya V2 prospectus/CIS title and CIS row 1 say Arya Health Insurance, but footer Product Name says Arya Group Health Insurance; all print retail UIN NHIHLIP27047V022627. Production card and wording support retail association.
findings.effect: Associate as conflicted retail companions, not as evidence merging individual/group families.

findings.finding: Aditi V1 post-hospitalization body says 60 days immediately preceding admission, table says 90 days post discharge. V2/V3 body says 90 days preceding while table says post discharge. V4 body says 90/180 preceding while plan table says post discharge. These are original conflicts, not corrected calculation constants.
findings.effect: Affected post-hospitalization capabilities need source clarification/explicit precedence before answer/calculation acceptance.

findings.finding: Arya retail V2 section 3.3(b) states 90 days for named networks; Annexure 1 has 180 days at Preferred/Verified and most eligible non-network cases, with 90 at Other Provider under Arya Plus.
findings.effect: Keep body and provider-specific table assertions; no universal 90/180-day result established.

findings.finding: Arya Group V1 table lists 25/50 lakh and 1 crore; V2 also lists Unlimited. Aditi V4 has Plan 1, Plan 2, Plus Plan; V6 has Plan 1, Plan 2, Plus, Prime, POS–Aditi and POS–Aditi Plus. V6 POS non-surgical sublimit is Not applicable, distinct from zero/unlimited.
findings.effect: Store plan/table selectors and limit state by version; do not carry later options into earlier policies.

findings.finding: Narayana Group V1/V4 schedule tables leave SI, room and many amounts/durations to issued Certificate of Insurance/Policy Schedule; V4 <selected option> is a placeholder. V4 post-hospitalization table and body also say before/preceding admission, whereas V1 table says post discharge.
findings.effect: Issued terms are materially required. Do not invent a default amount or convert placeholder into zero/unknown insurer rule.

findings.finding: Aditi V6 provider-table headers mix section 6(b)/(a) with 5(d)/(c); provider paragraph first refers to Verified and/or Other in 2C then distinguishes 2B/2C. Arya V2 grant points to Healthcare Provider section 6 although visible heading is section 5. Narayana Group V4 labels both Preferred and Verified as Annexure 2A.
findings.effect: Store exact references and proposed dependency resolution separately; connected original annexures must be read before rule publication.

findings.finding: Production register row 11 says policies between 28-Feb-2026 to 10-May-2026 onwards, retaining contradictory onwards. Historical register has earlier open-ended rows later bounded by production register. Every update-register row says Updated.
findings.effect: Append dated observations; do not overwrite historical assertions or infer withdrawal.

findings.finding: Four known revisions remain without located wordings: Aditi V5, Arya retail V1 and Narayana Group V2/V3. Source inspection found actual historical V1 group documents on public insurer staging, but no matching links for these four gaps.
findings.effect: Unperformed further discovery/insurer clarification, not an HTTP failure or proof of unavailability; rule denominators unknown.

acquisition_audit.full_query_provenance_handling: Full insurer-public signed blob URLs retained in private research provenance only; generated report and aggregate output use hashes/basenames.
discovery_paths: public insurer staging /product found by targeted official-domain search; staging source is not current production publication evidence
acquisition_audit.search_limit: Targeted search yielded production and insurer staging product pages; no exact missing-wording links were established. Search snippets were navigation only, not ingested contractual evidence.
acquisition_audit.staging_provenance_correction: The UAT HTML acquisition linking_url field used the production product URL as task navigation context; there was no observed production-to-UAT anchor. Actual discovery was official-domain web search. This explicit observation corrects provenance interpretation without altering immutable attempt.

generalized_information_requirements: Maintain separate exact title, footer, disclaimer, register-row and navigation-label assertions and document revisions; conflicts must not be silently merged.
Separate family, retail/group form, version, plan, optional cover, provider-network tier and issued schedule selections. A later UIN does not establish policy applicability or launch date.
Support finite money, explicit Unlimited, zero, Not applicable and unfilled issued-template placeholders as distinct states; enforce selected sublimit <= selected SI where the original says so.
Source dependency graphs must retain body/table disagreements and malformed connected-clause references with affected capabilities blocked until resolved.
Provider applicability depends on version, selected plan, emergency/planned treatment, travel/relocation evidence, intimation times and dated provider lists.
Buyer and insured identity, household/member ownership and issued certificate/schedule/underwriting evidence remain separate from public group or retail product documents.
Zero legacy rows never removes an original-roster insurer from corpus discovery, original-rule inventory and insurer-level acceptance requirements.

verification.pdf_visual_reading_notes: 23 full-page renderings manually inspected for table selectors, footers, original typos and native-text anomalies. MuPDF emitted seven No common ancestor in structure tree warnings during rendering; all 23 outputs were produced and visually inspected. These warnings and bounded native-text limits do not establish full parsing completeness.
verification.native_extraction_anomaly: V2 p25 contains hidden/repeated extraction text not visible in the rendering; the disclaimer evidence uses manually read visible transcription. Native whole-page text elsewhere is explicitly a reading aid, not a verified verbatim rendition of every glyph.
